topic: National Parks, Biosphere Reserves, and Wildlife Sanctuaries
description: To conserve India's rich biodiversity, the government has established a comprehensive network of Protected Areas. This network includes National Parks, Wildlife Sanctuaries, and Biosphere Reserves to protect endangered species and fragile ecosystems.

sections.title: Concept of Protected Areas and Legal Framework
sections.description: The classification of biodiversity conservation areas and the primary legal framework that governs them in India.

key_concepts.explanation: A strictly protected area where hunting, grazing, forestry, and human habitation are completely prohibited. Its boundaries are circumscribed by state or central legislation.
A species-specific protected area where limited human activities, such as minor forest produce collection and regulated grazing, are allowed provided they do not interfere with wildlife well-being.
A large protected landscape divided into Core, Buffer, and Transition zones. It aims to balance biodiversity conservation with the sustainable economic and social development of local communities.

historical_events.significance: A landmark legislation passed to ban poaching, protect endangered plant and animal species, and establish a legal framework for creating National Parks and Sanctuaries.

sections.title: Major National Parks of India
sections.description: Key National Parks across various Indian states renowned for their unique ecosystems and flagship species.

geographical_data.key_characteristics: Established in 1936 as Hailey National Park, it is the first National Park of India. The Ramganga River flows through it.
Located in the Brahmaputra River floodplains, it hosts two-thirds of the world's population of the Great One-horned Rhinoceros.
It is the only natural habitat of the Asiatic Lion in the entire world.
A UNESCO World Heritage Site famous for hosting winter migratory birds, most notably the Siberian Crane.
The largest contiguous mangrove forest in the world and the prime habitat of the Royal Bengal Tiger.

sections.title: Major Biosphere Reserves of India
sections.description: Prominent Biosphere Reserves recognized under the UNESCO Man and the Biosphere (MAB) Programme.

key_concepts.explanation: An intergovernmental scientific program launched by UNESCO to establish a scientific basis for the improvement of relationships between people and their environments.

geographical_data.key_characteristics: Established in 1986, it is India's first Biosphere Reserve. It is famous for the endangered Lion-tailed Macaque and Nilgiri Tahr.
India's first marine biosphere reserve in South and South-East Asia, renowned for the conservation of the Dugong (Sea Cow).
The highest biosphere reserve in India and the only 'Mixed' UNESCO World Heritage Site in the country.

sections.title: Important Wildlife Sanctuaries and Conservation Projects
sections.description: Crucial government initiatives and sanctuaries dedicated to the protection of highly vulnerable species.

historical_events.significance: Launched from Jim Corbett National Park to arrest the decline of the Bengal Tiger population and ensure their viable survival.
Launched as a Centrally Sponsored Scheme to protect elephants, their natural habitats, and migration corridors to prevent human-animal conflict.

geographical_data.key_characteristics: It is the world's largest known mass nesting site (called Arribada) for the endangered Olive Ridley sea turtles.
Located in the Cardamom Hills around Periyar Lake, it is highly renowned as an elephant and tiger reserve.

key_associations.extra_info: Located near Srinagar in Jammu & Kashmir, it is the only viable natural habitat of the critically endangered Hangul.

sections.title: Geographical Facts and Superlatives
sections.description: High-yield, exam-oriented superlatives and unique facts regarding India's protected area network.

important_facts.fact: Hemis National Park in Ladakh is the largest National Park in India and is globally famous for its high density of Snow Leopards.
South Button Island National Park in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands is the smallest National Park in India.
Keibul Lamjao National Park in Manipur is the world's only floating National Park, situated on Loktak Lake, and is the last home of the Sangai (Dancing Deer).
Among all Indian states, Madhya Pradesh holds the record for having the maximum number of National Parks.
